title: Many Shapes of Monster
tagline: the fourth boss - one loop, three kinds of enemy
hints: `class Goblin : public Monster` means a Goblin IS a Monster and gets everything Monster has.
A derived constructor passes up to the base with an initialiser list: `Goblin() : Monster("goblin", 12) {}` - the colon goes between the parentheses and the body.
`virtual` in the base means 'the derived class may replace this'. `override` in the derived means 'I am replacing something' - and the compiler checks you spelled it right.
Wraith deliberately does NOT override attackRoll. Leave it out and it inherits the base version, which is roll(4). That is inheritance doing its job.
`m->cry()` is the dot for pointers. Every `new` you write needs exactly one `delete`, and the delete loop goes at the very end of main.
